plan.title: test(windows): coverage-report symlink-swap test assumes O_NOFOLLOW (#7199 D)

narratives.Description: The controller.test.ts test 'symlink swap at the read (mocked lstatSync, no production hook): exit 4 row refused' fails on Windows because readCoverageReportNoFollow (packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/coverage-report.ts) has no O_NOFOLLOW there and falls back to lstat presence plus an fstat check, which the mocked lstat passes. This story decides the Windows behavior for a symlink swap at the coverage-report read, writes that decision in coverage-report.ts or the test, and makes the test pass on the nightly Windows lane by a platform skip with a reason or by a product fallback that refuses the swap, while the Linux nightly and the merge gate stay green.
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

`packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/controller.test.ts` > "waived arm reads the report without following a symlink > symlink swap at the read (mocked lstatSync, no production hook): exit 4 row refused" fails on Windows: `runObservablesComplete(...).ok` is `true`, expected `false`.

`readCoverageReportNoFollow` (`packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/coverage-report.ts:44`) opens the report with `O_NOFOLLOW`. Windows has no `O_NOFOLLOW`, so the code falls back to "lstat presence plus an fstat check on the opened fd". The test mocks `lstatSync` to report a regular file at the swapped path, so on Windows the fallback follows the symlink and accepts it. The Windows runner can create symlinks, so the test does not take its `EPERM` early return.

## Scope (1 file / 1 test)

- `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/controller.test.ts` (1).

## Likely fix site

Decide which side is wrong:
- If the no-follow guarantee is POSIX-only by design, the test skips on platforms without `O_NOFOLLOW` and says why.
- If Windows must refuse a swapped symlink too, the fallback in `coverage-report.ts` also compares the opened fd's identity with a fresh `lstat` (or checks for a reparse point) and refuses a mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Windows behavior for a symlink swap at the coverage-report read is decided, and the decision is written in `coverage-report.ts` or the test.
- [ ] The test passes on the nightly Windows lane, by a platform skip with a reason or by a product fallback that refuses the swap.
- [ ] The Linux nightly and the merge gate stay green.

Refs #7199, #7172
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer running the suite on Windows, I want the coverage-report symlink-swap test to follow a decided Windows behavior, so that the nightly Windows lane is green without silently weakening the no-follow read.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Decide the Windows behavior for a symlink swap at the coverage-report read: either the no-follow guarantee is POSIX-only (the test skips where O_NOFOLLOW is absent and says why) or the win32 fallback in readCoverageReportNoFollow refuses a swapped symlink (for example a reparse-point or fd-identity check, in coverage-report.ts or readRegularFileNoFollow in fs/contained-write.ts).
2. Write the decision as a comment in coverage-report.ts or the test.
3. Apply the matching change: a platform skip with a reason in controller.test.ts, or the product fallback plus a test in contained-write.test.ts or controller.test.ts.
4. Run the targeted tests on Windows and Linux; add one changelog.d fragment; regenerate RULE-MAP, PROJECT-DEFINITION, evaluator-surface disposition and the spec-drift row only if the build changes them.
